summary: Strengthen applied cracking, alkane unreactivity, and catalytic-converter practice while adding a reusable faded cracking example.

improvements.why: Cracking practice is mostly recognition; examiner reports note equations with unbalanced products.
improvements.what: Add two distinct exam-style Suggest questions: derive a possible shorter alkane and alkene pair from a heavy alkane by balancing both C and H, and assess whether a proposed product set conserves atoms and has lower $M_r$ products. Include full worked explanations and progressive hints.

improvements.where: pack worked and note, after existing cracking example
improvements.why: The note has one solved decane example but the pack has no worked/faded pair for transfer to another feedstock.
improvements.what: Add a stepwise cracking worked example with a faded variant using different formulas; explicitly check carbon and hydrogen balances and explain why the alkene product is useful.

improvements.why: Only six items cover this outcome and most repeat the same two claims without testing how bond strength and polarity separately explain resistance to polar attack.
improvements.what: Add an exam-style Explain question requiring both strong $\ce{C-H}$ bonds and their relative lack of polarity, plus an MCQ with distractors that confuse bond strength with bond polarity or attribute unreactivity solely to saturation.

improvements.why: Environmental questions mostly recall products and one converter equation; learners need to trace each exhaust pollutant through consequence and catalytic removal.
improvements.what: Add an applied multi-part item matching CO, nitrogen oxides and unburnt hydrocarbons to consequences and converter products, and an MCQ testing why converter use does not eliminate $\ce{CO2}$ emissions.
